frontmatter.title: Hadamard phase estimation with fresh preparations
frontmatter.description: Explicit repeated controlled powers, sine/cosine count data, bounded dyadic recovery and complete fresh-trial accounting.

children.value: An eigenphase becomes visible through interference with a control qubit. Measuring that control in two bases gives sine and cosine information; experiments at several powers resolve the aliases of an individual fringe. Classical processing replaces the coherent inverse QFT in this Hadamard-test/Kitaev-style route

Explicit primitive experiments, bounded dyadic angle recovery, independent matrix/probability checks and a twelve-output seeded study are executed. Each represented quantum trial has a fresh prepared target. Counts are sampled classically from checked ideal circuit probabilities; no QPU execution, native physical estimate, synthesized rotation sequence or Lean proof is supplied. The ideal confidence argument has exact-input/exact-real assumptions, while SDK and inverse-tangent checks remain numerical.

. An adapter must retain the actual initial resets, target preparation, every controlled gate, synthesis, data exposure, all repetitions and final readout. The static QDK adapter rejects resets, so dropping them to reuse its numbers would remove required work. A suitable instrument model must also allocate gate/reset/readout faults and probability bias at the same precision/confidence target.

The frozen surface-code baseline is unchanged. Factory/code-distance choices, rotation synthesis, routing and reset/controller timings have not been computed for this protocol. Ideal probability concentration cannot be transferred to approximate or noisy trials without a new systematic-error allowance and confidence calculation. Physical initialization, communication and compilation latency are unmeasured. There is no physical gain ratio against textbook or retained-target QPE.
Verification, record provenance and classical simulation

children.label: Verification, record provenance and classical simulation

children.value: The gate/operator checks cover normal-angle one-, two- and three-data-wire cases, sine signs, controlled scalar phases and explicit measured/reset instruments. Recovery tests include circular wrap, exact/integer fringes, zero-signal ambiguity, malformed counts and bounded iterable consumption. The confidence planner’s rational bound is compared with an independent high-precision decimal exponential.
; its source snapshots, counts, timings and manifest remain intact. The current source adds only a rejection guard for nonexact subnormal halving/underflow. A

authenticates that immutable producer, proves every canonical component bypasses the guard, reproduces all 49 QASM exports, performs numerical probability/operator checks for the 48 small circuits, checks register/resource evidence and recovers all twelve saved outputs. The larger nine-wire export remains source/count-only. Producer and replay source identities are recorded separately; the replay is not a new sampled experiment.
No formalization or Lean proof is reproduced for these circuits or recovery. The circuit, numerical inference, exact bound arithmetic and physical model are distinct evidence layers.
Use the locked Python 3.12 environment and complete public code package:

python scripts/verify_hadamard_qpe.py
python scripts/generate_hadamard_qpe.py --single --phase 0.3 --levels 6 \
  --output-dir artifacts/hadamard-new-run
python scripts/generate_hadamard_qpe.py --single --target-qubits 8 --levels 6 \
  --no-sim --output-dir artifacts/hadamard-large
pytest tests/test_hadamard_qpe.py tests/test_hadamard_qpe_generator.py \
  tests/test_hadamard_qpe_record.py
executes saved replay and gate checks. Optional controls check gate probabilities and run new bounded experiments in a local/Binder kernel. Set
in that kernel to enable them; static publication keeps them disabled and needs no public backend.

literal calls per individual experiment, 200,000 operations per circuit/schedule and 64 distinct experiments per generator invocation. Confidence workloads stop at 100,000 represented trials per producer; output stops at 64 MiB with a 180-second generator allowance. Dense references stop at three data wires. Stored nonzero phase components must permit exact binary64 halving; unsupported subnormal/underflow inputs are rejected. These guards are separate from a scalable-performance guarantee.
